newsitem.title: USA: Aon seeks acquisition, but won't be rushed.
newsitem.headline: Aon seeks acquisition, but won't be rushed.

text.p: Aon Corp, flush with roughly $1 billion in cash from the sale of two of its life insurance businesses earlier this year, said it wants to spend the money on an insurance brokerage or consulting acquisition, but won't be rushed into a bad deal.

Rumors linking Aon with just about every major insurance broker have proliferated in the nine months or so since Aon announced agreements to sell Life Insurance Co of Virginia and Union Fidelity Life Insurance Co to General Electric Co's GE Capital Corp.
And some Wall Street analysts and bankers, who had expected Aon to strike some sort of deal by now, speculated that Aon might buy back stock instead.
But Aon spokesman William Fasel said the company does not intend to buy back stock.
"That has not been our stated objective. Our stated objective has been to redeploy the money into core operations and to grow the business, not shrink it," he said.
Meanwhile, he said, Aon is simply taking its time to carefully review potential acquisitions, not just for attractive financial terms, but for strategic and cultural fit as well.
But market speculation has intensified in recent weeks after two major brokers said they were willing to consider their strategic alternatives.

In mid-August, Sedgwick Group Plc put itself forward as a possible merger candidate and two weeks later St. Paul Cos Inc essentially put its Minet Group insurance brokerage on the market when it said it retained Goldman Sachs to assist it in examining strategic alternatives for Minet.
Talk at the reinsurance industry's annual rendezvous in Monte Carlo this week linked Aon with Sedgwick.
Aon said it could not confirm or deny the rumor, but said an announcement was not imminent.
"I don't think at this point we're looking to announce anything," he said.

"We look at the spectrum and it will most likely evolve according to the way we want to proceed not to the way others are going to push us to proceed, so therefore there's uncertainty as to timing," he said.
But some analysts said a merger with Sedgwick might make sense if Aon wants to expand its presence internationally.
"They're acquisition strategy in the brokerage area has been a global one," an industry source said. But he said he would not rule out either an international or domestic acquisition.
However, "Sedgwick would probably even out Aon's premium distribution from a global standpoint," he said.
In addition, Aon was believed to have cast its eyes toward London before. Aon late last year was reportedly in talks that later fell through to buy Bain Hogg from parent group Inchcape Plc.
And Aon, ranked second in terms of gross revenues according to a July 1995 Business Insurance survey, would get a boost in size from an acquisition of third-ranked Sedgwick.
But Aon's Fasel said the company is not focused strictly on size but wants to be "one of the few worldwide quality operations."
And Aon certainly has sufficient funds available to it to buy just about any broker it wants, analysts said.
Aside from Marsh & McLennan Cos Inc and Johnson & Higgins, which is a private partnership, "just about everybody else might be within reach," the industry source said.
